:::writing{variant="social_post" id="41827"}
Question for the longevity-focused practices...

Are peptides still an "add-on" in your clinic, or have they become a meaningful revenue center?

I'm seeing a huge difference between practices that simply offer peptides and practices that have built a true longevity program around them.

The second group seems to be creating:
• Better retention
• Longer patient relationships
• Higher patient lifetime value
• More referrals

Curious what everyone is seeing. Have peptides become a significant part of your business yet?
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="65192"}
Something I've noticed recently...

Patients are starting to ask fewer aesthetic questions and more health optimization questions.

They want to know:
• How to age better
• How to recover faster
• How to improve energy
• How to preserve muscle
• How to optimize long-term health

It feels like the line between aesthetics and longevity is getting blurrier every day.

For those of you offering longevity services, what are patients asking for most right now?
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="38415"}
I'm curious...

What percentage of your patients currently participate in some form of wellness, longevity, peptide, HRT, weight loss, or optimization program?

Not what you'd like it to be.

What is it today?

I've found many practices have far more interest in these services than they realize, but they aren't actively tracking it.

Would love to hear where everyone is landing.
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="72064"}
Hot take:

The most valuable patient in a med spa over the next 5 years may not be the filler patient.

It may be the longevity patient.

Someone who engages monthly, invests in their health, stays connected to the practice, and views you as a long-term partner rather than a one-time provider.

Are you seeing that trend in your clinic, or am I completely off base?
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="58371"}
For practices offering peptides...

What has surprised you the most?

Not clinically.

From a business perspective.

Has it been:
• Retention?
• Revenue?
• Compliance?
• Patient demand?
• Education challenges?

I'm seeing some clinics generate incredible patient engagement through peptides and longevity programs, while others struggle to get traction.

Interested in hearing real-world experiences.
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="91743"}
If you were starting a med spa from scratch in 2026, would you build it around aesthetics or longevity?

Not saying one is better than the other.

But if you had to choose where the next decade of growth is headed, where would you place your bet?

I'd love to hear perspectives from owners who are actively seeing patient behavior shift.
:::

These work particularly well because they attract exactly the owners who are already thinking about peptides, HRT, weight loss, wellness, and longevity. Those are the same owners who tend to be most interested in a Revenue Leak Audit because they're looking for ways to increase patient lifetime value rather than just buy more leads.

The best posts for med spa owner groups are the ones that spark curiosity and conversation—not the ones that sound like you're prospecting. Given Luxora's new positioning around Revenue Leak Audits and hidden revenue, I'd focus on observations and questions.

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="58214"}
Curious...

How many med spa owners know exactly how much revenue they're losing each month from patients who already said "yes" once?

Not leads.

Not marketing.

Existing patients.

The more practices I look at, the more I realize the biggest growth opportunities are usually hiding inside:

• Lapsed patients
• Membership gaps
• Consultation no-shows
• Underutilized treatment plans
• Missing follow-up systems

Most owners immediately think they need more leads when what they really need is better visibility.

What's the biggest revenue blind spot you've discovered in your practice?
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="73195"}
I have a question for med spa owners...

If I could wave a magic wand and add an extra $100,000 in revenue to your practice this year, where do you think it would come from?

A) More leads
B) Better conversions
C) Better retention
D) Higher patient spend
E) Memberships

I've been digging into practices lately and the answers are rarely what owners expect.

Would love to hear everyone's thoughts.
:::

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="26483"}
Unpopular opinion:

Most med spas don't have a lead problem.

They have a systems problem.

I've seen practices spending thousands on ads while sitting on years worth of inactive patients, unbooked consultations, and missed follow-up opportunities.

The irony?

Fixing those issues is usually faster, cheaper, and more profitable than buying more traffic.

What do you think is the most overlooked growth lever in aesthetics right now?
:::

**Bonus tip:** Don't pitch in the comments. Let people engage. Then when someone says, "I'd love to know where my leaks are," reply with:

*"Happy to take a quick look for you. Shoot me a DM and I'll share a few things I'd check first."*

That converts far better than dropping a Calendly link.
